concepts.gloss: Coordination is a structure whose coordinates have equal syntactic standing, with neither assigned head or dependent function.
Coordination with three or more bare coordinates at the level being analysed.
Coordination without an overt coordinator, potentially harder to distinguish from non-coordination.
Multiple syndetic coordination where only the final coordinate bears a coordinator.
Multiple syndetic coordination where each coordinate after the first bears a coordinator.
A bare coordinate in multiple coordination that is neither initial nor final.
Syndetic coordination with a correlative determinative such as both or either on the first coordinate.
Syndetic coordination lacking an initial correlative determinative.
The core coordinate constituent excluding any coordinator or coordinate-related modifiers.
The larger coordinate constituent incorporating the bare coordinate and its marker and/or modifiers.
Cambridge's analysis in which the coordinator forms a constituent with the following coordinate and its possible modifiers.

rules.statement: A coordination with precisely two bare coordinates is binary, while one containing more than two bare coordinates in the same structure is multiple.
rules.condition: Classify a coordinative construction by its number of bare coordinate constituents: exactly two yields binary coordination and three or more at one level yields multiple coordination, independently of whether a coordinator is overt.

contrast.text: A designer and an engineer reviewed the prototype. [binary NP-coordination]
A designer, an engineer, and a researcher reviewed the prototype. [multiple NP-coordination]
The door opened and the alarm rang. [binary clause-coordination]
They will travel by car, by train, or by ferry. [multiple PP-coordination]

rules.review_notes: The source contrasts binary with multiple by number of coordinates. Do not confuse the number of coordinators with the number of coordinates. Owner expressly approved required Chapter 15 changes on 2026-11-05; no independent second-pass AI review took place.

rules.statement: A coordination is syndetic when it is overtly linked by a coordinator and asyndetic when its coordinate relation is expressed without an overt coordinator.
rules.condition: For an independently identified coordination, inspect whether a syntactic coordinator such as and or or marks the construction; classify overtly coordinated instances as syndetic, and unmarked series as asyndetic, without assuming all comma-separated phrases must be coordinations.

contrast.text: They consulted the architect and the engineer. [syndetic NP-coordination]
They consulted the architect, the engineer. [asyndetic series in an appropriate list context]
The guests laughed, the host smiled. [asyndetic clause-coordination]
The guests laughed and the host smiled. [syndetic clause-coordination]

rules.statement: Multiple syndetic coordination is simple-syndetic when only the final coordinate has a coordinator, and polysyndetic when each non-initial coordinate is marked by a coordinator.
rules.condition: For a single-layer multiple coordination of three or more bare coordinates, examine the coordinators before the second, medial and final coordinates: final-only marking is simple-syndetic and marking before every non-initial coordinate is polysyndetic.

contrast.text: The workshop is scheduled for Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday. [simple-syndetic]
The workshop is scheduled for Tuesday or Thursday or Saturday. [polysyndetic]
They ordered soup, rice, and vegetables. [simple-syndetic]
They ordered soup and rice and vegetables. [polysyndetic]

rules.concept: uniform coordinator marking of medial coordinates in single-layer multiple coordination
rules.statement: In a single-layer multiple syndetic coordination, medial bare coordinates must be marked consistently: either none is marked or all are marked.
rules.condition: In a multiple coordination of four or more bare coordinates analysed at one syntactic layer, with a coordinator marking the final coordinate, apply one marking pattern to all medial coordinates; mixing marked and unmarked medial coordinates violates the described unlayered construction.
rules.violation: At least one medial coordinate in the same single-layer coordination has an overt coordinator while another medial coordinate in that layer lacks one.

correct.text: They can meet on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday. [all medial coordinates unmarked]
They can meet on Monday or Tuesday or Wednesday or Friday or Saturday. [all medial coordinates marked]
The choices were tea, coffee, lemonade, or water. [final-only pattern]

incorrect.text: *They can meet on Monday or Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday. [mixed medial markers if analysed as one layer]
*They can meet on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, Friday or Saturday. [mixed medial marking in a proposed single-layer analysis]

rules.statement: Correlative coordination marks the initial coordinate with a determinative paired with the final coordinator, such as both with and or either with or; the corresponding non-correlative coordination lacks the initial marker.
rules.condition: For a syndetic coordination, identify an optional initial correlative determinative paired with the final coordinator: both is paired with and, and either with or. Either may also occur with both simple-syndetic and polysyndetic multiple coordination.

Either on Tuesday or on Thursday works for us. [correlative either...or]
The event may run either on Tuesday, on Thursday, or on Saturday. [multiple simple-syndetic with either]
The event may run either on Tuesday or on Thursday or on Saturday. [multiple polysyndetic with either]

rules.concept: coordinator as marker within the following expanded coordinate
rules.statement: In Cambridge's constituent analysis, a coordinator is a marker within the coordinate that follows it, rather than an independent head governing two coordinates.
rules.condition: For a syndetic construction, group the coordinator and the following bare coordinate into an expanded coordinate; the grouping is supported by their remaining adjacent in end-attachment variants and by prosodic breaks or punctuation preceding the coordinator.

contrast.text: The director or her deputy will present the report. [or her deputy forms an expanded coordinate]
The director will present the report, or her deputy. [end-attached coordinate retains or]
The team approved the design, and the client signed it. [punctuation before and]
And the client signed it. [sentence-initial coordinator with its following clause in a discourse continuation]

rules.statement: A bare coordinate is the core coordinate constituent; an expanded coordinate also contains its coordinator and/or modifying expressions such as indeed, too, or as well.
rules.condition: When analysing a coordinate containing an overt marker or coordinate-oriented modifiers, distinguish the constituent supplying the bare coordinate from its larger expanded coordinate, which includes any attached coordinator and pre- or post-coordinate modifiers.

contrast.text: The agency praised the volunteers and the organisers. [the organisers: bare coordinate]
The agency praised the volunteers and especially the organisers too. [and especially the organisers too: expanded coordinate]
We invited the curator and indeed the archivist as well. [and indeed the archivist as well: expanded coordinate]
The artist thanked the audience, her family too. [asyndetic expanded coordinate with too]
